prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opening moire quantum matter

statement.case_for: I keep B028 as the whole prize. After the full first-round exchange the case rests on three things that nobody has disputed. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model made a quantitative, falsifiable prediction in 2011 that the lowest bands flatten at a specific twist angle. The 2018 experiments of Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle. And independent groups have reproduced the phases and extended them across many moire systems, with interaction strength tuned by a gate and an angle rather than by chemistry. The chair's summary records that no member disputes that the flat bands and the correlated phases are real, so the open question is interpretation, not existence. I would word the citation around flat bands and correlated states and not around the pairing mechanism, which keeps the prize on what has been measured and reproduced. This is also scientifically distinct from the 2025 prize and from the earlier topological-phase prize. My view has not changed from round 1, but the exchange has tested it and I hold it with moderate rather than high confidence.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is maturity: the experiments date from 2018, the origin of the superconductivity and of the correlated insulators is unsettled, and Kroll and Danielsson are right that a more mature candidate such as B022 is safer on timing. The second objection is credit. Yuan Cao and the other first authors, and the Dean and Young groups on related moire systems, are outside the three names, and Bistritzer's inclusion consumes the whole three-person allowance. If the committee judged that either problem could not be repaired in a citation, B022 would be a defensible alternative, and it is a cleaner two-name allocation.

responses.point: Kroll keeps B022 as a single prize, arguing for Katori's magic-wavelength concept and Ye's 10^-18 programme as a clean, mature two-person case, and holds B028 as an alternative on maturity.
responses.response: I accept that B022 is the better case on attribution and independent confirmation, and I would not oppose it. We differ on what the clock case shows today: the constants tests and dark-matter searches give bounds, not yet a discovery, whereas flat-band moire physics has already changed what condensed-matter groups measure and compute. On maturity I read the question as whether the discovery is secure, not whether every mechanism is closed. Fractional quantum Hall physics was honoured while its interpretation was still developing. I do take your point that the unsettled superconductivity is a real risk, which is why my citation avoids it.

responses.point: Danielsson moved from B037 to a two-part B002 plus B022 prize and now says the committee would need a clear principle for crediting detector architects before B037 can carry a prize.
responses.response: I agree that no such principle has been agreed. I also would not support the pairing of B002 with B022 as the preferred outcome. It combines a single-name credit for a collaboration-scale discovery with a clock prize because their supporters overlap, and Lindroth has made the same objection. Your own reservation that the clock's reach is prospective argues for pairing it with a discovery in the strict sense, but I would not choose a partner whose credit the committee cannot yet state. I have therefore kept B037 only as a second alternative, conditional on the principle being settled.

responses.point: Mehlig sees the unsettled pairing mechanism in B028 as not disqualifying, because the prize would honour the platform discovery, and he accepts that B022 is cleaner on attribution.
responses.response: I share your view that the prize honours the platform and not the pairing theory, and I would hold the citation to that. Where I would add a caution to your own argument is that it applies equally to B001, whose interface mechanism is still debated, so the maturity test cannot be applied to B028 alone. I agree with you that B028 has a real attribution disadvantage against B022, and I would not use breadth of ballot support as the argument.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, pairs B002 and B022, asks whether Halzen alone can carry a part, and said B014 would be better served by waiting after the 2025 prize.
responses.response: On B014 I now agree with you and have kept it out of both my preferred configuration and my alternatives, both because of the proximity to 2025 and because the four-name credit list does not resolve Girvin against Blais. On B002 the chair's own question is the one I cannot answer: I have no basis from the supplied record to say that conception and leadership by one person is the decisive credit, and I would want the external experts to confirm the AMANDA to IceCube history. Until that is done, I do not think B002 should carry a part of the prize.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B028 alone with three names but says the question of whether Bistritzer belongs with MacDonald is open, and asks for a persuasive three-person allocation.
responses.response: I keep Bistritzer. The 2011 paper was written by Bistritzer and MacDonald, and it is the one that fixed the magic angle; omitting him would leave the theory credit incomplete. Dropping him would also leave one place free that we could not then use for Cao or any other experimentalist, since the experimental credit sits with the group leader under the usual practice. I would ask you whether, as a correlated-electron theorist, you see a stronger case for a two-name version.

responses.point: Olsson now ranks B028 first, argues that discovery security is separate from mechanism, and notes twist-angle inhomogeneity is now directly mapped in devices.
responses.response: I agree with your distinction and the microscopy point is useful, because it narrows one of the main concerns about reproducibility. I would not rely on it too heavily, since device-to-device variation remains a real feature of the phase diagram and the committee should say so honestly in the citation. Thank you also for disclosing the shared Chalmers affiliation, which I confirm below.

uncertainties: Whether the unresolved origin of superconductivity makes the prize premature this year even though the flat bands and correlated phases are reproduced.
Whether Bistritzer should be named with MacDonald, and whether Cao and the Dean and Young groups can be acknowledged in the citation within the three-name limit.
Whether the committee, which has no agreed principle for large collaborations, would be better served by the two-name B022 as a safer single prize.
I rely on general knowledge, not on the supplied evidence, for the dates and roles of the credited people.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. My research field is circuit and waveguide QED, I direct WACQT at Chalmers, and I have Chalmers colleagues and collaborators in that area, so I keep B014 and other superconducting-circuit candidates out of my configuration and alternatives. My profile shows no specific connection to B028, B022 or B037. I confirm the institutional link noted by Olsson, who is also at Chalmers, but I know of no shared project with any shortlisted candidate or credited person.
